Fig. 2. Overview of the SASA framework. (Top) Semantic Anchor Learning employs rigid anchors (At) and elastic residual tokens (Rt) under orthogonality and magnitude constraints to prevent feature drift. (Bottom) Spatial Label Arbitration utilizes a class-agnostic segmentor to resolve supervision conflicts between Yold and Ynew , generating denoised pseudo-labels for spatially coherent incremental learning. Segmentation logits are computed from the similarity between pixel features and class tokens in Eq. 2, without a separate mask decoder; SLA is only used during training.

Fig. 1. Illustration of Feature Drift vs. Stabilized Learning. (Left) Merging sparse cues with hallucinations creates Contradictory Supervision, causing new classes to overwrite the old ones (Feature Drift). (Right) We propose Spatial Label Arbitration to denoise labels via object masks. Combined with Rigid Anchors and Elastic Residual Tokens (ERTs), our SASA maintains a stable, drift-resilient feature space throughout incremental steps.
